answer: Treat the economy as a trust graph where each agent is a vertex and edges come only from completed, paid jobs between two parties. Rewards flow by short random walks from long-standing seed agents, so a sybil cluster of any size touches honest agents through only a handful of real edges and receives little weight. Inside the cluster fake trades look velvet-smooth, yet they add no paths from the seeds, and buying real edges leaves an onyx-dark trail of payments that auditors can trace.
